perf.CORRECTION_r10: THE JS-FRAME-TIME HALF OF THIS ROUND'S PERF HEADLINE WAS NOISE, AND IT WAS MY NUMBER. I wrote '7.6 ms worst frame vs landscape's 2.5' into the note below as evidence that portrait was over every bar. The round-10 perf owner showed the statistic does not exist: shoot.mjs's `cpu.max` is the single worst of 400 samples from an UNSEEDED loop and swings 8.5x between two back-to-back runs of ONE build on one machine (1.8 ms and 15.3 ms, shots/r10-perf vs shots/r10-perf-rep). Re-shooting r9's own code today gave 6.6 landscape / 3.8 portrait -- THE SIGN REVERSED. Attributed with a labelled rig the spikes land on steps where nothing happens (no spawn, no cut), i.e. GC/JIT, not the game. The stable statistics (median, p95) were under the 2.0 ms bar in BOTH orientations before and after. WHAT WAS REAL: the draw-call and triangle halves. 187 calls / 267k tris portrait against 120 / 250k ceilings reproduced on every re-shoot and are now fixed (115 / 160k). WHAT WAS NOT: the JS-time claim. Recorded here rather than quietly edited out, because this is the fourth invalid metric in three rounds and the first one that was mine.

note:
Round 9 was built before the weekly usage limit and critiqued after it, so the two halves are 9 days apart; the builds and the frames are unchanged between them. Four of five critiques are in and every one of them raises the score: stage 73 -> 78, fruit-geo 73 -> 76, fruit-mat 68 -> 73, juice 70 -> 74. Cutter 72 -> 76. Mean 71.2 -> 75.4, mean delta +4.2, the largest of any round so far and the first round in which all five pieces moved together. Four of the five report their PREVIOUS round's headline gap as closed or substantially closed on the shipped frames in BOTH orientations, which is the first time that has happened in nine rounds. Stage: the r8 two-sided band (filament reads the streak core, glare reads the skirt, so it cannot be gamed from one side) is met simultaneously on the hero and on the portrait beat the r8 critic named as the worst frame in either directory. Juice: the heavy-tail statistic area_p95_over_median reaches plate-01 for the first time (hero 6.37 -> 8.66 vs 8.36), and the ellipse-congruence tell open since round 5 is closed on 04-cut+250ms.

THE MOST IMPORTANT EVENT THIS ROUND IS NOT A SCORE — IT IS THAT TWO CRITICS RETRACTED THEIR OWN PUBLISHED NUMBERS, AND ONE RETRACTION HAD THE WRONG SIGN. The fruit-mat critic — the same agent that wrote the r8 verdict — WITHDREW ITS OWN R8 HEADLINE NUMBER after the builder refused it. The r8 window `foam win=262:352:88:160` did not measure the cut face at all: on portrait the largest luma component in that window is the WHOLE melon half and the ellipse centre lands on green rind. The frozen probe says so itself with no extra machinery — pct_lum_le_25 is 4.96 landscape against 22.74 portrait on the identical statistic. Re-cited onto a face-centred window the finding changes. A builder refused a critic's number, the critic re-measured, agreed, and retracted in writing. That is the loop working the way it was supposed to, and it is worth more than the +5.

The cutter critic then did the same thing harder, and its retraction is the single most useful measurement
result of the project so far: it withdrew TWO r8 numbers and one of them POINTED THE WRONG WAY. r8-cutter
had reported `collar ridge_width_px_med / sqrt(mask_px)` at 0.03922 against plate-01's 0.02812 and
concluded the collar band was 39% too WIDE. Run the identical frozen probe on the identical plate at three
resolutions — same content, pure Lanczos resample — and the statistic swings 2.9x on ONE image with
nothing changed: 0.02812 native, 0.06818 at 640 wide, 0.08253 at 405. Mask-matched, our r9 collar is
43-46% too NARROW. The opposite sign. The critic also caught itself about to publish a second one — it had
written 'the collar is blown out' from `collar.pct_R_ge_255` 37.78 vs plate-640's 5.00, then ran the plate
NATIVE and got 28.89, because downsampling a photograph 2.6x destroys clipping. Both statistics were
dropped. THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES, and it now belongs beside the geometric-mask rule at the top of
probes.py: A PROBE IS ONLY VALID AGAINST A REFERENCE AT MATCHED SCALE, and normalising by sqrt(mask_px)
does not make a pixel-domain statistic scale-invariant. Nine rounds of cross-resolution plate comparisons
are suspect wherever the statistic has a pixel-sized kernel. The measurements that survive are the ones
where the resample works AGAINST the finding.

A third retraction landed on top of those two: three verdicts, two of them cutter's own, had called the cut
cap a radial starburst. The fruit-mat critic's new `spokes` probe retracted it and the cutter critic
independently reproduced and seconded the retraction. Three rounds of builder effort were spent on an
artefact that was not in the pixels.

TWO INSTRUMENT/BUDGET PROBLEMS REMAIN OPEN AND BOTH ARE NOW CONFIRMED BY A SECOND PARTY.
(1) PORTRAIT IS OVER EVERY PERF BAR: 187 draw calls vs a 120 bar, 267k triangles vs 250k, 7.6 ms worst frame vs landscape's 2.5 — on the only configuration that ships. Every perf number this project has reported for nine rounds was landscape, so the budget has been defended on the wrong device throughout. Same disease as the portrait-only visual defects: a threshold expressed in pixels is correct at one raster and wrong at another.
(2) THE identity METRIC I ADDED IN ROUND 8 IS SATURATED, and the round-9 geometry critic supplied the decisive number rather than the qualitative one I had: in r8 the ORANGE was provably featureless — `limb pose=so3 n=32` gives hull_concave_frac_pct EXACTLY 0.00, boundary_cv_median 0.008, elongation_median 1.011, a convex sphere in all 32 poses — and its identity_recall was 1.000. identity awards a PERFECT SCORE TO A MATHEMATICAL SPHERE. It is a 6-way closed-set 1-NN whose only referent is the other five bodies, all of which we authored. So identity stays as a CONTROL (it is not gameable by deletion the way separation was, and it caught the builder's kiwi/melon spur collision) and is retired as a TARGET. The critic also tried to build the external referent from plate-01 and reports that it DOES NOT WORK BY AUTO-SEGMENTATION; the negative result is measured and written into probes.py so round 10 does not repeat it. Self-consistency cannot measure resemblance to a real apple — that needs a referent outside the thing being measured, exactly as the mask rule did.

AND A THIRD, WHICH THE GEOMETRY CRITIC FOUND AND WHICH IS THE REAL SILHOUETTE STORY: every outline event this project has ever authored sits ON THE POLAR AXIS — calyx, stem, crown, navel, spur — so a fruit is nameable only in the poses that happen to show a pole. Doubling the apple calyx (0.110 -> 0.225) moved the isolated pose sweep hard (hull_concave_frac_pct 41.80 -> 50.78) and moved the SHIPPED pixels barely at all landscape (24.22 -> 25.78) and DOWNWARD portrait (62.50 -> 59.38), because in neither shipped pose is a pole toward camera. Round 10's geometry work is equatorial, not polar.

pieces.name: Lighting, grade & DOF
pieces.biggestGap: The streak's core never bleaches: plate-01's rim streak is achromatic white at the core (core saturation p50 0.045, core RGB like [241,243,241], peak p50 237.4) with the orange living only in the halo, while ours is a saturated amber rod from end to end (core sat p50 0.445 hero / 0.451 portrait, core RGB [212,152,111], peak p50 177.4) -- and it went the WRONG WAY this round, 0.353 -> 0.445, because the soft ceiling at stage.js ~2350 is deliberately hue-preserving (applied to the max channel with the ratio carried through), which is exactly the mechanism that stops an over-driven warm source from clipping to white the way a real sensor does.
pieces.fix: src/render/stage.js, the SOFT CEILING block (~2338-2352), one expression. Today `kn = fCeil*(1-exp(-pk/fCeil))/pk` is computed from `pk = max(lit.r,lit.g,lit.b)` and multiplied into all three channels, so the core's hue is invariant to brightness and the streak can never bleach. Make the knee PER-CHANNEL -- `lit.rgb -> fCeil*(1-exp(-lit.rgb/fCeil))` component-wise -- which is the same curve, the same ceiling, and the same behaviour for everything dim, but lets R saturate before G and G before B so an over-driven warm source goes white at the core with an amber fringe, exactly as plate-01 does. Then, and only then, restore the near half's radiance so it actually reaches that ceiling: the near stations peak at 130/161/162 against plate-01's 226/241/234, so the head-room is real, and the cheapest lever is `fApA` (0.45) and/or `fKappa` back up from 0.25 toward the middle, both of which you already have sweeps for. Do NOT reach for `fWarm` -- the wing hue is right (wing sat 0.939 vs plate 0.388 is only a consequence of the core being coloured too). ACCEPTANCE, frozen suite, on the shipped hero AND shots/r9-iphone/04-cut+250ms, quoting all of these together because any one alone is gameable: core saturation at the `_radon_ridge` peak, p50 over 13 stations, from 0.445/0.451 down UNDER 0.15 (plate-01 0.045) with at least 8 of 13 stations under 0.10; `lens` ribbon peak p50 from 177/171 up over 215 (plate-01 237.4); WHILE HOLDING everything round 9 won -- `filament flattop_p50` inside 0.29-0.34 (today 0.333/0.293), `glare u05_u50_p50` inside 1.4-2.1 (today 1.953/1.924) and `u20_u50_p50` inside 1.30-1.55 (today 1.463/1.429), `lens` ribbon peak_max_over_min <= 1.8, `void` corner_max <= 3.0 on 01-whole-watermelon in both orientations (today 2.93/2.98), and the worst single-pixel wing drop at hero x=1208/1066/924 under 1.40 (today 1.35/1.30/1.31). pieces.fix: src/fruit/geometry.js — PUT A FEATURE ON THE EQUATOR. The file's own 5A theorem names three mechanisms that can reach a silhouette (axis ratios, plane cuts, appendages) and this piece now uses two of them, both of which live at or near the polar axis; the result is item 3, a large mesh gain that no shipped pose displays. Add the third as a per-species ANGULAR modulation of the profile radius, r(theta, y) = r(y) * (1 + a_k * cos(k*theta + phase(y))), applied in the existing lathe loop for ZERO extra triangles and with star-shapedness preserved by construction (r is still single-valued in theta, so cutter.js's precondition and `star_multivalued_total` 0 are safe). Concretely: apple k=5, a=0.05-0.07 with phase drifting ~0.15 rad from calyx to stem — real apples are genuinely five-lobed in cross-section and it is the one apple cue that survives every pose; kiwi k=2, a=0.06 (a real kiwifruit's section is an ellipse, not a circle); strawberry k=3, a=0.04 on the shoulder band only. Pre-empting the objection: the r5 relief corollary (T^2/8 caps a bump at 0.14% of radius) is about ~3 degrees of arc and does NOT bind a 72-degree lobe, so do not cite it here. THEN CHANGE THE GATE. Give the collar band a torn EDGE, and take the edge modulation TANGENTIALLY, not radially.
